data.narrative:
Nabla Bio is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Surge Biswas and Frances Anastassacos, operating within a competitive frontier biotech landscape. The valuation universe comprises 3 public Biotech & Health comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Valuation analysis relied on a single applicable method due to data constraints. Stage-progression analysis anchored to Nabla's $37M total capital raised, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage progression, yielding $74M. Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable; while 7 same-sector peers exist, no sufficiently tight peer cohort (requiring ≥3 companies matching stage, adjacency, or valuation tier) materialized. Public-comp anchoring using the sector's 9.2x P/S median (across 3 tickers) could not proceed without disclosed target revenue, a chronic limitation for private-company analysis.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $63M to $85M, centered on $74M. This range reflects downside/upside variance around the single stage-progression method rather than true triangulation. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight private peer data, undisclosed revenue, and the applicability of 2.0x step-up multipliers to this particular stage and market cycle. Additional diligence on unit economics and partnership monetization of the $1.5B+ partnership commitments would strengthen conviction.
